**Section 6.01 Conduct of Business Prior to Closing**

**(a)** From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), except as (i) required by applicable Law, (ii) set forth on Schedule 6.01, or (iii) consented to in writing by Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), Seller shall cause the Company to:
> \(i\) conduct its business in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice in all material respects;

> \(ii\) use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve intact its business organization, relationships with customers, suppliers, licensors, licensees, Governmental Authorities, and other Persons with whom the Company has material business relationships, and to retain its current officers, key employees, and other key personnel;
> \(iii\) maintain in full force and effect all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate; and
> \(iv\) maintain its books and records in accordance with past practice and in compliance with applicable Laws.

**(b)** Without limiting the generality of Section 6.01(a), from the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), except as (i) required by applicable Law, (ii) set forth on Schedule 6.01, or (iii) consented to in writing by Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), Seller shall not permit the Company to:
> \(i\) amend, modify, or restate the articles of incorporation, bylaws, or other organizational documents of the Company;

> \(ii\) issue, sell, transfer, pledge, dispose of, grant, or authorize the issuance, sale, transfer, pledge, disposition, or grant of any shares of capital stock, or any options, warrants, convertible securities, or other rights to acquire any shares of capital stock, of the Company;

> \(iii\) declare, set aside, authorize, make, or pay any dividend or other distribution (whether in cash, stock, property, or otherwise) in respect of any shares of capital stock of the Company, or repurchase, redeem, or otherwise acquire any shares of capital stock of the Company;
> \(iv\) incur, assume, guarantee, or become liable for any Indebtedness in an amount in excess of \$250,000 individually or \$750,000 in the aggregate;

> \(v\) make any capital expenditures in excess of \$500,000 individually or \$1,500,000 in the aggregate, other than capital expenditures contemplated by the Company\'s approved capital expenditure budget previously provided to Buyer;

> \(vi\) enter into, materially amend, modify, terminate, waive any material rights under, or renew any Company Material Contract (other than renewals in the ordinary course of business on substantially similar terms);

> \(vii\) (A) hire or engage any employee or independent contractor with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000, (B) terminate (other than for cause) any employee with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000, or (C) increase the compensation or benefits of any employee or independent contractor (other than annual merit-based increases in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice for employees earning less than \$150,000 per year);

> \(viii\) settle, compromise, or consent to the entry of judgment in any Action involving payments by or to the Company in excess of \$200,000 or that would impose any non-monetary obligation on the Company;
> \(ix\) change any method of accounting or accounting practice, principle, or policy, except as required by changes in GAAP or applicable Law;

> \(x\) make, change, or revoke any material Tax election, settle or compromise any material Tax claim, audit, or assessment, file any amended Tax Return, or enter into any agreement with a Governmental Authority with respect to Taxes;

> \(xi\) sell, lease, transfer, license, abandon, permit to lapse, or otherwise dispose of any material assets or properties of the Company (other than sales of inventory or obsolete equipment in the ordinary course of business);
> \(xii\) grant, create, incur, assume, or suffer to exist any Encumbrance on any material asset or property of the Company (other than Permitted Encumbrances); or
> \(xiii\) enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement.
**Section 6.02 Access to Information**

From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), Seller shall, and shall cause the Company and its officers, directors, employees, accountants, counsel, and other Representatives to, upon reasonable prior notice, afford Buyer and its Representatives reasonable access during normal business hours to the Company\'s properties, offices, plants, other facilities, books, records, contracts, documents, and personnel, and shall furnish to Buyer and its Representatives such additional financial, operating, and other information regarding the Company as Buyer may reasonably request; *provided* that (a) such access shall not unreasonably interfere with the normal operations of the Company, (b) such access shall be conducted in a manner that preserves the confidentiality of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (c) Seller shall not be required to grant access to, or furnish, any information the disclosure of which would (i) violate any applicable Law, (ii) jeopardize any attorney-client privilege or other legal privilege, or (iii) contravene any binding obligation of confidentiality, and (d) all information provided pursuant to this Section 6.02 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Confidentiality Agreement.
**Section 6.03 Confidentiality**

The Mutual Confidentiality Agreement, dated as of June 20, 2025, between Seller and Buyer (the \"Confidentiality Agreement\") shall continue in full force and effect in accordance with its terms, and the terms of the Confidentiality Agreement are hereby incorporated herein by reference. If this Agreement is terminated prior to the Closing, the Confidentiality Agreement shall survive such termination in accordance with its terms.
**Section 6.04 HSR Act Filings**

**(a)** Each of Buyer and Seller shall, as promptly as practicable (and in no event later than ten (10) Business Days after the date of this Agreement), file or cause to be filed with the United States Federal Trade Commission and the United States Department of Justice all notifications and other documents and information required to be filed under the HSR Act with respect to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(b)** Buyer and Seller shall each use their reasonable best efforts to (i) obtain early termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act, (ii) comply at the earliest practicable date with any request for additional information and documentary material that may be issued under the HSR Act, (iii) cooperate with the other Party in connection with any filing under the HSR Act and in connection with resolving any investigation or other inquiry of any Governmental Authority under the HSR Act, and (iv) take all actions necessary, proper, or advisable to cause the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act as promptly as practicable.
**(c)** Buyer shall pay all filing fees payable under the HSR Act in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(d)** Each Party shall promptly notify the other Party of any substantive communication with, and any inquiry from, any Governmental Authority in connection with the HSR Act filings, and shall provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on any substantive written communications to any such Governmental Authority prior to submission.
**Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents**

Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, as promptly as practicable following the date of this Agreement, all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, including those set forth on Schedule 4.05. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Seller and the Company in connection with obtaining such consents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Seller nor the Company shall be required to pay or commit to pay any amount to (or incur any obligation in favor of) any Person from whom any such consent or waiver may be required (other than filing, application, or similar fees imposed by any Governmental Authority).
**Section 6.06 Public Announcements**

Neither Party shall, and each Party shall cause its respective Affiliates not to, issue any press release or make any public announcement relating to the subject matter of this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); *provided* that either Party may make any public disclosure that it believes in good faith is required by applicable Law, any listing or trading agreement concerning its publicly traded securities, or any rule or regulation of any securities exchange or self-regulatory organization, in which case the disclosing Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to advise the other Party prior to making the disclosure and to provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment upon such disclosure.
**Section 6.07 Tax Matters**

**(a)** *Pre-Closing Tax Returns.* Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be prepared and timely filed) all Tax Returns of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period that are due (taking into account any valid extensions) after the Closing Date. All such Tax Returns shall be prepared in a manner consistent with past practice (unless otherwise required by applicable Law). Seller shall provide drafts of such Tax Returns to Buyer for its review and comment at least thirty (30) days prior to the due date for filing (or, if such Tax Return is due less than forty-five (45) days after the Closing Date, as soon as reasonably practicable). Seller shall consider in good faith any reasonable comments provided by Buyer. Seller shall timely pay or cause to be paid all Taxes shown as due and payable on such Tax Returns.

**(b)** *Straddle Period Tax Returns.* For any taxable period that includes, but does not end on, the Closing Date (each, a \"Straddle Period\"), the Taxes of the Company attributable to the portion of such Straddle Period ending on and including the Closing Date (the \"Pre-Closing Straddle Amount\") shall be determined using a \"closing-of-the-books\" methodology as of the end of the Closing Date, except that Taxes imposed on a periodic basis (such as real property Taxes) shall be allocated to the Pre-Closing Straddle Amount based on the number of days in the Straddle Period falling on or before the Closing Date relative to the total number of days in such Straddle Period.

**(c)** *Transfer Taxes.* All transfer, documentary, sales, use, stamp, registration, value-added, and other similar Taxes and fees (including any penalties and interest) imposed in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (collectively, \"Transfer Taxes\") shall be borne equally by Buyer and Seller. The Party required by applicable Law to file the Tax Return with respect to any Transfer Tax shall file such Tax Return in a timely manner, and the other Party shall promptly reimburse such filing Party for its allocable share of such Transfer Tax.

**(d)** *Cooperation.* After the Closing, Buyer and Seller shall cooperate fully, as and to the extent reasonably requested by the other Party, in connection with the filing of Tax Returns of the Company and the conduct of any audit, litigation, or other proceeding with respect to Taxes of the Company. Such cooperation shall include the retention and, upon the other Party\'s request, the provision of records and information that are reasonably relevant to any such Tax Return, audit, litigation, or other proceeding, and making employees available on a mutually convenient basis to provide additional information and explanation of any material provided hereunder.

**(e)** *Tax Elections.* Neither Buyer nor the Company shall, without the prior written consent of Seller (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), (i) make or change any Tax election with respect to the Company that would have retroactive effect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period, (ii) amend any Tax Return of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period, or (iii) initiate any voluntary disclosure or similar proceeding with any Governmental Authority with respect to any Pre-Closing Tax Period.
**Section 6.08 Employee Matters**

**(a)** For a period of not less than twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, provide each employee of the Company who continues in employment with the Company following the Closing (each, a \"Continuing Employee\") with (i) base salary or wages at least equal to the base salary or wages provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing, and (ii) employee benefits that are, in the aggregate, substantially comparable to those provided to such Continuing Employee immediately prior to the Closing. Nothing in this Section 6.08 shall be construed to guarantee employment for any specific period of time, to restrict Buyer\'s or the Company\'s right to terminate the employment of any employee, or to create any third-party beneficiary rights in favor of any employee.

**(b)** With respect to any Employee Benefit Plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, credit each Continuing Employee with his or her years of service with the Company (and any predecessor entities) prior to the Closing Date for purposes of eligibility to participate, vesting, and benefit accrual (but not for purposes of benefit accrual under any defined benefit pension plan).

**(c)** Buyer shall, or shall cause the Company to, permit each Continuing Employee who participates in the Company\'s 401(k) plan to roll over his or her account balance under such plan into a tax-qualified defined contribution plan maintained by Buyer or the Company following the Closing, in accordance with applicable Law.
**Section 6.09 Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation**

**(a)** *Non-Competition.* For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict Seller or its Affiliates from (i) owning, directly or indirectly, solely as a passive investment, securities of any Person that are traded on a national securities exchange if Seller and its Affiliates do not, directly or indirectly, beneficially own five percent (5%) or more of any class of securities of such Person, or (ii) performing its obligations under this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents.

**(b)** *Non-Solicitation.* For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, (i) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage (or attempt to solicit, recruit, hire, or engage) any employee of the Company, or (ii) solicit or encourage (or attempt to solicit or encourage) any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship of the Company to cease or reduce its business with the Company; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict (A) general solicitations of employment not specifically directed toward employees of the Company, including through advertisements in newspapers, trade journals, or online job boards, or (B) solicitations by headhunters or recruiting firms not specifically directed by Seller or its Affiliates to target employees of the Company.

**(c)** *Remedies.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of any of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 6.09 would cause irreparable damage to Buyer and the Company and that monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. Accordingly, in the event of any actual or threatened breach by Seller or any of its Affiliates of the provisions of this Section 6.09, Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive relief (temporary, preliminary, and permanent) from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. The restrictive covenants contained in this Section 6.09 are independent of any other provision of this Agreement, and the existence of any claim or cause of action of Seller against Buyer, whether predicated on this Agreement or otherwise, shall not constitute a defense to the enforcement of such restrictive covenants.
**Section 6.10 Directors\' and Officers\' Insurance**

For a period of six (6) years following the Closing Date, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain in effect directors\' and officers\' liability insurance (\"D&O Tail Insurance\") covering acts or omissions occurring at or prior to the Closing Date with respect to those Persons who are or were directors or officers of the Company at or prior to the Closing Date, on terms (including coverage amounts, retentions, and other material terms) that are no less favorable in the aggregate than the D&O insurance maintained by the Company as of the date of this Agreement; *provided* that the annual premium for such D&O Tail Insurance shall not exceed 250% of the annual premium currently paid by the Company for its existing D&O insurance.
**Section 6.11 Further Assurances**

From time to time following the Closing, each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances, and take such further actions as may be reasonably required to carry out the provisions of this Agreement and the other Transaction Documents and to give effect to the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby.

**[CONDITIONS TO CLOSING]{.underline}**
**Section 7.01 Conditions to Each Party\'s Obligations**

The respective obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable Law, waiver by each Party) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
**(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.

**(c)** No Action by any Governmental Authority shall be pending that seeks to (i) restrain, enjoin, prevent, prohibit, or make illegal the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) impose limitations on the ability of Buyer to effectively exercise full rights of ownership of the Shares, or (iii) compel Buyer or any of its Affiliates to dispose of or hold separate all or a material portion of the business or assets of the Company.
**Section 7.02 Conditions to Buyer\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* (i) The Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date); and (ii) each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" or \"Material Adverse Effect\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except, in the case of this clause (ii), where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.

**(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* Since the date of this Agreement, no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence shall have occurred that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.02(a), 7.02(b), and 7.02(c) have been satisfied.
**(e)** *Seller Deliverables.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(a).
**(f)** *Third-Party Consents.* All consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.
**(g)** *Escrow Agreement.* The Escrow Agreement shall have been duly executed and delivered by Seller and the Escrow Agent.
**Section 7.03 Conditions to Seller\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Seller) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* Each representation and warranty of Buyer contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the ability of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Buyer shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Buyer under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.

**(b)** any breach or nonperformance of any covenant or agreement of Buyer contained in this Agreement.
**Section 9.04 Limitations on Indemnification**

**(a)** *Basket.* Seller shall not be obligated to indemnify any Buyer Indemnitee for Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) until the aggregate amount of all such Losses exceeds the Basket Amount (\$2,150,000), and then only for Losses in excess of the Basket Amount (it being understood and agreed that the Basket Amount shall operate as a true deductible and not as a \"tipping\" or \"first-dollar\" basket).

**(b)** *Cap.* The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap (\$43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

**(c)** *Fundamental Representations.* The limitations set forth in Sections 9.04(a) and 9.04(b) shall not apply to Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations. The aggregate liability of Seller for Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price (as finally determined pursuant to Section 2.04).

**(d)** *Escrow as Source of Recovery.* With respect to claims for indemnification under Section 9.02(a) (other than claims arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations), the Escrow Fund shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for all Losses up to the Escrow Amount (\$16,125,000). Claims for Losses under Section 9.02(a) (other than claims arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) in excess of the Escrow Amount may be pursued directly against Seller, subject in all cases to the Indemnification Cap and the other limitations set forth in this Section 9.04.

**(e)** *Insurance Offset.* The amount of any Losses subject to indemnification under this Article IX shall be reduced by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received by the indemnified party (net of any costs of collection and any increases in premiums directly attributable to such claim) with respect to such Losses. Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to recover under applicable insurance policies for any Losses for which it seeks indemnification hereunder.

**(f)** *Tax Benefits.* The amount of any Losses subject to indemnification under this Article IX shall be reduced by the amount of any Tax benefit actually realized (through a reduction of cash Taxes payable) by the indemnified party or its Affiliates in the taxable year in which such Losses are incurred or in the immediately succeeding taxable year.

**(g)** *Mitigation.* Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate any Losses for which indemnification may be sought under this Article IX. No indemnifying party shall be liable for any Losses that the indemnified party could reasonably have avoided or mitigated.

**(h)** *No Duplication.* No indemnified party shall be entitled to recover the same Losses more than once under multiple provisions of this Agreement or any other Transaction Document. Without limiting the foregoing, any Losses that are reflected in the final determination of the Purchase Price pursuant to Section 2.04 shall not give rise to a claim for indemnification under this Article IX.
**Section 9.05 Indemnification Procedures**

**(a)** *Notice of Claim.* An indemnified party seeking indemnification under this Article IX shall promptly deliver to the indemnifying party a written notice (a \"Claim Notice\") specifying in reasonable detail (i) the nature of the claim, (ii) the factual basis for such claim, (iii) the sections of this Agreement upon which such claim is based, and (iv) the amount of Losses claimed (or, if not then ascertainable, a reasonable estimate thereof). The failure to deliver a Claim Notice promptly shall not relieve the indemnifying party of its indemnification obligations, except to the extent (and only to the extent) that the indemnifying party is actually and materially prejudiced by such failure.

**(b)** *Third-Party Claims.* If any Action is commenced or threatened by any third party against an indemnified party (a \"Third-Party Claim\"), the indemnified party shall promptly deliver a Claim Notice to the indemnifying party. The indemnifying party shall have the right, at its sole cost and expense, to assume the defense of any Third-Party Claim by delivering written notice thereof to the indemnified party within thirty (30) days after receipt of the Claim Notice; *provided* that (i) the indemnifying party acknowledges in writing that it has an indemnification obligation with respect to such Third-Party Claim (subject to the limitations set forth in this Article IX), (ii) the Third-Party Claim involves only monetary damages and does not seek injunctive or other equitable relief against the indemnified party, (iii) the indemnified party has not been advised by counsel that a conflict of interest exists between the indemnified party and the indemnifying party with respect to such Third-Party Claim, and (iv) the Third-Party Claim does not relate to or arise in connection with any criminal or quasi-criminal proceeding, action, indictment, allegation, or investigation. If the indemnifying party assumes the defense of a Third-Party Claim, the indemnified party shall have the right to participate in the defense thereof and to employ counsel, at its own expense, separate from the counsel employed by the indemnifying party. The indemnifying party shall not settle, compromise, or consent to the entry of any judgment with respect to any Third-Party Claim without the prior written consent of the indemnified party (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); *provided* that such consent shall not be required if the settlement (A) involves only the payment of monetary damages for which the indemnifying party has acknowledged indemnification liability and (B) includes an unconditional release of the indemnified party from all liability arising out of such Thi... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

**(c)** *Direct Claims.* With respect to any claim for indemnification that does not involve a Third-Party Claim (a \"Direct Claim\"), the indemnifying party shall have thirty (30) days after receipt of the Claim Notice to respond thereto. If the indemnifying party does not respond to a Direct Claim within such thirty (30) day period, the indemnifying party shall be deemed to have accepted such Direct Claim and the indemnified party shall be entitled to recover the amount of Losses set forth in the applicable Claim Notice.
**Section 9.06 Effect of Knowledge**

Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.
**Section 9.07 Exclusive Remedy**

Following the Closing, except in the case of fraud, the indemnification provisions set forth in this Article IX shall constitute the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parties and their respective Affiliates and Representatives for any breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement or in any certificate delivered pursuant hereto, and for any other claim arising out of or relating to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, whether based upon contract, tort, strict liability, or otherwise. Nothing in this Section 9.07 shall limit (a) any Party\'s right to seek specific performance or injunctive relief in accordance with Section 10.10, (b) any Party\'s right to assert claims based on fraud, or (c) any Party\'s rights or remedies under Section 2.04 (Post-Closing NWC Adjustment) or Section 2.05 (Earnout).
**Section 9.08 Escrow Releases**

**(a)** *General Release.* On the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, the Escrow Agent shall release to Seller from the Escrow Fund an amount equal to the balance of the Escrow Fund at such time, minus the aggregate amount of all pending but unresolved indemnification claims for which Claim Notices have been delivered to Seller and the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 9.05 (such withheld amount, the \"Pending Claims Reserve\").

**(b)** *Final Release.* With respect to any portion of the Escrow Fund retained as a Pending Claims Reserve, such amounts shall continue to be held in the Escrow Fund until (i) final resolution of the applicable pending claims in accordance with this Article IX or (ii) the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date with respect to claims relating to Fundamental Representations. Upon the final resolution of each pending claim, the Escrow Agent shall promptly release (A) to Buyer, the amount of Losses finally determined to be payable to Buyer Indemnitees with respect to such claim, and (B) to Seller, the excess, if any, of the Pending Claims Reserve attributable to such claim over the amount released to Buyer under clause (A).

96: >
97: > \(f\) Changes affecting the industries in which the Company operates generally; and
98: >
99: > \(g\) Changes resulting from the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by the agreement.
100: 
101: **These carve-outs are acceptable only if they include a \"disproportionate impact\" qualifier.**
102: 
103: **THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** All industry-specific carve-outs and regulatory carve-outs in the MAE definition MUST include a \"disproportionate impact\" exception. This is a firm-wide requirement and is non-negotiable for environmental services transactions. The standard formulation the firm requires is:
104: 
105: > *\"\...provided, however, that any change, effect, event, or development referred to in clauses (a) through (f) above shall be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur to the extent such change, effect, event, or development disproportionately affects the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate.\"*
106: 
107: **Rationale.** Without the disproportionate impact qualifier, industry-specific and regulatory carve-outs can effectively hollow out the MAE definition, rendering it meaningless. This risk is especially acute for environmental services companies. Consider the following scenario: if the MAE definition carves out \"changes in environmental laws or regulations\" or \"changes affecting the environmental services industry generally\" without a disproportionate impact qualifier, the seller could argue that virtually any adverse regulatory development --- including a new CERCLA regulation that specifically targets the target\'s disposal practices, a state-level ban on a waste treatment methodology that constitutes 40% of the target\'s revenue, or an EPA enforcement initiative directed at the specific category of environmental services the target provides --- is excluded from the MAE definition because it \"affects the environmental services industry generally\" or constitutes a \"change in environmental law.\" This interpretation would render the buyer\'s closing condition (no MAE since signing) essentially unenforceable, because the most likely sources of material adverse change for an environmental services company are precisely the regulatory and industry changes that the carve-out would exclude.
108: 
109: The disproportionate impact qualifier resolves this problem by providing that even if a change is of the type described in the carve-out (e.g., a general change in environmental law), it still counts toward the MAE analysis to the extent it disproportionately affects the target compared to other industry participants. This preserves the buyer\'s protection against target-specific harm while still excluding truly general, industry-wide developments that affect all participants equally.
110: 
111: **Specific Instruction.** If the seller\'s draft excludes \"changes in the environmental services industry generally\" or \"changes in environmental laws or regulations\" from the MAE definition without a disproportionate impact qualifier, this MUST be flagged and corrected. The associate should add the disproportionate impact qualifier language set forth above. **Priority: CRITICAL.**
112: 
113: **Example of Acceptable MAE Carve-out Language:**
114: 
115: > *\"\...provided, however, that none of the following shall be deemed to constitute, and none of the following shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect: (a) changes in general economic conditions or conditions in the financial markets generally; (b) changes affecting the industries in which the Company operates generally; (c) changes in applicable Law (including Environmental Laws) or GAAP; (d) acts of war, armed hostilities, terrorism, or natural disasters; (e) epidemics, pandemics, or other public health emergencies; or (f) changes resulting from the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated hereby; provided, further, that, with respect to clauses (a) through (e), such changes, effects, events, or developments may be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur to the extent that such changes, effects, events, or developments have a disproportionate effect on the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to other participants in the industries in which the Company and its Subsidiaries operate.\"*
116: 
117: **[2.2 Environmental-Sector-Specific MAE Considerations]{.underline}**
118: 
119: Beyond the general requirement for the disproportionate impact qualifier addressed in Section 2.1, associates must be attentive to several additional MAE issues that are unique to environmental services acquisitions.
120: 
121: **Regulatory Exposure.** Environmental services companies are uniquely exposed to regulatory changes that could devastate the target\'s value. Changes in CERCLA regulations, modifications to RCRA permitting requirements, new EPA enforcement policies, state-level environmental law changes, and shifts in regulatory interpretation can fundamentally alter the target\'s business model, cost structure, and liability exposure. A broadly worded regulatory carve-out without a disproportionate impact qualifier would allow the seller to argue that sweeping regulatory changes affecting the target --- even those directed specifically at the target\'s business practices --- are excluded from the MAE definition. This is precisely the scenario the disproportionate impact qualifier is designed to address, and its importance in the environmental services context cannot be overstated.
122: 
123: **Pending or Threatened Litigation.** Associates should carefully review whether the MAE definition carves out \"changes resulting from pending or threatened litigation.\" In many general middle-market transactions, this carve-out is unremarkable. However, for environmental services targets with known environmental exposure --- including targets that are potentially responsible parties (\"PRPs\") at CERCLA Superfund sites, targets with ongoing state environmental enforcement actions, or targets facing private contribution or cost-recovery claims --- a litigation carve-out could exclude from the MAE definition precisely the type of adverse development most likely to occur. If the target has known environmental litigation exposure, the associate should either (a) remove the litigation carve-out entirely, or (b) add an express exclusion to the litigation carve-out providing that it does not apply to environmental litigation or claims arising under CERCLA, RCRA, or state environmental law equivalents.
124: 
125: **CERCLA Exposure.** Specifically, exposures of the type associated with CERCLA response cost liability --- such as EPA information requests under CERCLA Section 104(e), PRP notification letters, unilateral administrative orders, and contributions to Superfund remediation costs --- should not be carved out of the MAE definition. These \"Dalton Creek-type\" CERCLA exposures (referring to the category of historical disposal site liabilities frequently encountered in environmental services due diligence) represent some of the most significant and unpredictable risks to environmental services companies, and the buyer must retain the ability to invoke the MAE closing condition if such liabilities materialize or escalate between signing and closing.
126: 
127: **Associates should confirm** that the MAE definition, read as a whole, does not inadvertently exclude from the MAE analysis the categories of adverse developments most relevant to the environmental services target being acquired. If in doubt, escalate to the responsible partner.
128: 
129: **[Section 3: Interim Operating Covenants (Pre-Closing Conduct of Business)]{.underline}**
130: 
131: **[3.1 General Framework]{.underline}**
132: 
133: The SPA must contain robust interim operating covenants restricting the target\'s conduct of business during the period between the signing of the SPA and the closing of the transaction (the \"Interim Period\"). During the Interim Period, the buyer bears economic risk (through the binding obligation to close, subject to closing conditions) but does not yet have control of the target. The interim operating covenants serve as the buyer\'s primary contractual protection against value leakage or deterioration during this period.
134: 
135: The standard interim operating covenants the firm requires include the following:
136: 
137: > \(a\) Operate the business in the ordinary course consistent with past practice in all material respects;
138: >
139: > \(b\) Use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain and preserve intact the business, operations, and relationships of the Company, including relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, and governmental authorities;
140: >
141: > \(c\) Maintain all insurance policies (including environmental impairment liability insurance) in full force and effect;
142: >
143: > \(d\) Maintain all properties and assets in good working condition (ordinary wear and tear excepted);
144: >
145: > \(e\) Comply in all material respects with all applicable laws, permits, and governmental orders;
146: >
147: > \(f\) Not enter into, amend, or terminate any material contract outside the ordinary course of business without buyer\'s prior written consent;
148: >
149: > \(g\) Not amend the Company\'s organizational documents (certificate of incorporation, bylaws, operating agreement, etc.);
150: >
151: > \(h\) Not make any capital expenditures in excess of an agreed threshold (typically \$250,000 individually or \$500,000 in the aggregate) without buyer\'s prior written consent;
152: >
153: > \(i\) Not hire, terminate, or change the compensation of any employee earning above an agreed threshold (typically \$150,000 annually) without buyer\'s prior written consent;
154: >
155: > \(j\) Not make any acquisitions of assets or businesses, or any dispositions of assets outside the ordinary course;
156: >
157: > \(k\) Not incur any indebtedness for borrowed money or guarantee any obligations of any third party;
158: >
159: > \(l\) Not create, incur, or permit any liens on the Company\'s assets (other than permitted liens); and
160: >
161: > \(m\) Not declare or pay any dividends or make any distributions to shareholders (other than tax distributions in the case of pass-through entities, subject to agreed limitations).
162: 
163: For environmental services targets, additional sector-specific covenants are required, as set forth in Section 3.3 below. Additionally, affiliate transaction restrictions --- which are critically important in this sector --- are addressed separately in Section 3.2 below.
164: 
165: Associates should review the seller\'s draft interim covenants against this list and flag any missing items. Sellers frequently attempt to limit the buyer\'s consent rights by omitting specific restrictions or by inserting broad \"ordinary course\" qualifiers that dilute the restrictions. Resist these efforts and maintain the specificity of the covenant package.
166: 
167: **[3.2 Affiliate Transaction Restrictions]{.underline}**
168: 
169: **THIS IS A HIGH-PRIORITY REQUIREMENT.** The interim operating covenants MUST include a specific, express restriction prohibiting the target from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, or terminating any contract, transaction, or arrangement with the seller, any affiliate of the seller, or any officer, director, manager, member, shareholder, or family member of the seller or any seller affiliate, without the buyer\'s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed).
170: 
171: **Rationale.** In acquisitions of family-owned or closely held environmental services targets, affiliate transactions represent a persistent and significant risk during the Interim Period. The selling shareholders and their affiliated entities frequently engage in transactions with the target that may not be at arm\'s length, and the risk of value extraction through affiliate transactions is heightened during the period between signing and closing, when the seller knows that it will shortly be relinquishing control of the business. Common abuses observed in environmental services transactions handled by the firm include:
172: 
173: > \(a\) **Increasing rent payments under affiliate leases.** Environmental services companies frequently lease office space, equipment yards, vehicle storage facilities, or waste disposal facilities from entities controlled by the selling shareholders. The seller may attempt to increase the rent under these leases during the Interim Period, extracting value from the target before the buyer takes control.
174: >
175: > \(b\) **Entering into new management or consulting agreements with seller-affiliated entities.** Sellers may attempt to create new contractual payment obligations running from the target to seller affiliates during the Interim Period, often styled as \"management fees,\" \"consulting arrangements,\" or \"transition services.\"
176: >
177: > \(c\) **Prepaying obligations to affiliates.** The target may accelerate payment of amounts owed to seller affiliates, depleting the target\'s cash and reducing net working capital.
178: >
179: > \(d\) **Extending the term of above-market affiliate contracts.** The seller may attempt to lock in above-market affiliate arrangements for extended periods, making them more difficult or expensive for the buyer to unwind post-closing.
180: 
181: **Specific Context for Environmental Services Deals.** In environmental services transactions, it is extremely common for the target to lease critical operational facilities --- including equipment yards, staging areas, waste storage facilities, and disposal sites --- from entities controlled by the selling shareholders. EBITDA adjustments for above-market affiliate rent are among the most common adjustments in this sector, with recent transactions handled by the firm reflecting above-market rent adjustments of \$1,600,000 or more. However, these EBITDA adjustments only protect the buyer on the purchase price (valuation) side --- they do not prevent the seller from increasing or adding affiliate payments during the Interim Period, which would reduce the target\'s cash flow and working capital independent of the valuation adjustment.
182: 
183: The affiliate transaction restriction covenant is the primary contractual mechanism to prevent this form of value leakage. Its inclusion in the SPA is mandatory. **Priority: HIGH.**
184: 
185: **Sample Affiliate Transaction Restriction Covenant:**
186: 
187: > *\"During the period from the date of this Agreement until the earlier of the Closing Date and the termination of this Agreement in accordance with its terms, the Company shall not, and Seller shall cause the Company not to, directly or indirectly, (a) enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, (b) amend, modify, extend, renew, or supplement any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with, (c) make any payment or transfer any asset to (other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice), or (d) terminate any existing Contract with, in each case, Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, shareholder, member, partner, or family member (within the meaning of Section 267(c)(4) of the Code) of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, in each case without the prior written consent of Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed).\"*
188: 
189: **[3.3 Environmental-Sector-Specific Covenants]{.underline}**
190: 
191: In addition to the general interim operating covenants set forth in Section 3.1 and the affiliate transaction restrictions set forth in Section 3.2, the SPA for an environmental services acquisition must include the following sector-specific interim covenants:
192: 
193: > \(a\) **Environmental Permits.** Maintain all Environmental Permits in full force and effect; do not take any action, or fail to take any action, that could reasonably be expected to result in the revocation, suspension, modification, non-renewal, or material limitation of any Environmental Permit held by the Company.
194: >
195: > \(b\) **Active Remediation Projects.** Continue all active remediation and environmental response projects in the ordinary course of business and in compliance with all applicable orders, consent decrees, administrative agreements, remediation action plans, and other governmental requirements. Do not voluntarily suspend, terminate, or materially alter the scope of any active remediation project without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
196: >
197: > \(c\) **New Environmental Remediation Contracts.** Do not enter into any new environmental remediation or response contract or agreement with a contract value exceeding \$500,000 (or such other threshold as may be agreed) without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
198: >
199: > \(d\) **Environmental Insurance.** Maintain all environmental impairment liability insurance policies, pollution legal liability insurance policies, and contractor\'s pollution liability insurance policies in full force and effect, with coverage levels no less than those in effect as of the date of the agreement.
200: >
201: > \(e\) **Notice of Environmental Claims.** Provide prompt written notice to the buyer (and in no event later than five (5) business days after the Company\'s receipt thereof) of any new environmental claim, notice of violation, information request under CERCLA Section 104(e), RCRA Section 3007, or any analogous state law provision, consent order, administrative complaint, or other regulatory action received by the Company during the Interim Period.
202: >
203: > \(f\) **Settlement of Environmental Claims.** Do not settle, compromise, or consent to the entry of any judgment with respect to any environmental claim, proceeding, or regulatory action involving potential liability in excess of \$250,000 (or such other threshold as may be agreed) without the buyer\'s prior written consent.
204: 
205: Associates should review the environmental due diligence memo for a list of all active remediation projects, environmental permits, and pending environmental claims, and confirm that the interim covenants adequately cover each identified item.
206: 
207: **[Section 4: Representations and Warranties --- Survival Periods]{.underline}**
208: 
209: **[4.1 General Survival Framework]{.underline}**
210: 
211: The survival period for representations and warranties determines the window during which the buyer may assert indemnification claims for breaches of those representations. The survival framework is one of the most commercially significant elements of the indemnification structure and must be carefully reviewed in every transaction.
212: 
213: The firm\'s standard survival framework for PE acquisitions in the environmental services sector is as follows:
214: 
215: **Fundamental Representations.** Representations relating to organization and existence, authority and enforceability, capitalization and equity ownership, no conflicts with organizational documents, and brokers and finders fees (collectively, \"Fundamental Representations\") must survive for the longer of (a) the full applicable statute of limitations (including any extensions or tolling periods) or (b) six (6) years post-closing. This survival period is non-negotiable. Fundamental Representations go to the core of the transaction --- whether the seller has the authority to sell what it purports to sell, and whether the buyer is getting what it is paying for. Abbreviated survival periods for Fundamental Representations are never acceptable.
216: 
217: **Tax Representations.** Representations relating to tax matters must survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations for the assessment of the relevant tax (including any extensions, waivers, or tolling periods). This extended survival period reflects the fact that tax authorities may audit and assess additional taxes well beyond the typical representation survival period. This survival period is non-negotiable and should not be shortened.
218: 
219: **General Representations.** All other representations and warranties (other than Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, and Environmental Representations, which are addressed in Section 4.2 below) should survive for a period of eighteen (18) to twenty-four (24) months post-closing. The market range for general representation survival in middle-market PE transactions is fifteen (15) to twenty-four (24) months. A survival period within this range is acceptable. A survival period below fifteen (15) months should be pushed back, as it provides the buyer with insufficient time to discover breaches, particularly breaches that may not become apparent until the buyer has operated the business through a full annual cycle. The firm\'s preferred position is twenty-four (24) months.
220: 
221: **Independence of Basket and Survival.** Associates should note that the basket (deductible) structure is independent of the survival period. Claims must be asserted during the applicable survival period (i.e., the buyer must provide written notice of a claim before the survival period expires), but the basket is a separate limitation on recovery that operates independently. A claim timely asserted during the survival period is not extinguished merely because the aggregate basket threshold has not yet been met; rather, timely-asserted claims accumulate and become recoverable once the basket threshold is satisfied.
222: 
223: **Basket Standard.** For reference (this topic is addressed in detail in Section 5.2), a true deductible of 0.75% to 1.0% of enterprise value is market-standard for middle-market transactions in the environmental services sector. A basket within this range should generally be accepted without markup, as discussed further in Section 11.2.
224: 
225: **[4.2 Environmental Representations --- Extended Survival]{.underline}**
226: 
227: **THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** For targets in the environmental services sector, environmental representations --- including but not limited to representations regarding environmental compliance, Environmental Permits, hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, CERCLA and Superfund matters, environmental remediation obligations, environmental insurance, and environmental litigation --- MUST survive for a minimum of thirty-six (36) months post-closing. The firm\'s preferred position is survival for the full applicable statute of limitations (which, for CERCLA claims, is effectively indefinite, as CERCLA imposes strict, joint and several liability with no statute of repose in many circumstances).
228: 
229: **Rationale.** Environmental liabilities under CERCLA, RCRA, and state environmental law equivalents frequently take years --- and in some cases, decades --- to manifest fully. The lifecycle of a typical CERCLA enforcement action illustrates this point:
230: 
231: > \(a\) EPA issues a CERCLA Section 104(e) information request to a potentially responsible party, seeking information about the party\'s waste disposal practices at a particular site. This initial inquiry may occur years after the disposal activity took place.
232: >
233: > \(b\) Following investigation, EPA may issue a general notice letter identifying the party as a PRP and inviting participation in a settlement process. This step may occur one to three years after the initial information request.
234: >
235: > \(c\) Negotiations with EPA and among PRPs regarding allocation of remediation costs may take an additional one to three years.
236: >
237: > \(d\) Remediation itself may span five to fifteen years, with ongoing cost disputes and contribution actions among PRPs throughout the process.
238: 
239: Given this timeline, a twelve-month survival period for environmental representations in an environmental services acquisition is grossly inadequate and well below market expectations for this sector. A buyer who discovers a previously undisclosed CERCLA exposure fifteen months after closing --- a timeline that is entirely typical --- would have no indemnification recourse under a twelve-month survival provision. This outcome is unacceptable for PE buyer clients and does not reflect the risk profile of the sector.
240: 
241: **Specific Instruction.** If the seller\'s draft provides for a general twelve-month or shorter survival period that applies to environmental representations without differentiation, this MUST be flagged and corrected. At minimum, environmental representations should be carved out of the general representation survival period and given an independent survival period of thirty-six (36) months post-closing. Ideally, push for survival for the full applicable statute of limitations. If the seller resists the full statute of limitations, thirty-six months is the firm\'s minimum acceptable position. **Priority: CRITICAL.**
242: 
243: **Coordination with Escrow Release.** The environmental representation survival period must be coordinated with the escrow release schedule (see Section 5.4 below). Escrow funds designated for environmental representation claims should not be released before the expiration of the environmental representation survival period. If the general escrow is scheduled for release at eighteen (18) months post-closing but the environmental representation survival extends to thirty-six (36) months, the SPA must provide for a separate environmental escrow holdback that is maintained through the thirty-sixth month (less any amounts reserved for pending claims).
244: 
245: **Coordination with Special Indemnity.** The environmental representation survival period is separate from and in addition to the Special Indemnity for known environmental liabilities (see Section 6 below). The Special Indemnity addresses specifically identified environmental matters with a separate seventy-two (72) month survival period. The environmental representation survival period addresses breaches of the environmental representations generally --- i.e., undisclosed environmental liabilities and inaccuracies in the environmental representations that are not covered by the Special Indemnity.
246: 
247: **[Section 5: Indemnification Structure]{.underline}**
248: 
249: **[5.1 Indemnification Cap]{.underline}**
250: 
251: **THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** The general indemnification cap is one of the most significant economic terms in the SPA and must conform precisely to the executed term sheet.
252: 
253: **Firm Standard.** For middle-market PE acquisitions in the \$100 million to \$500 million enterprise value range, the general indemnification cap should be set at 10% to 15% of the base enterprise value. The firm\'s target for PE buyer clients is 12.5% of enterprise value. This percentage represents the firm\'s standard recommendation based on extensive experience in environmental services transactions and is consistent with prevailing market data for the sector.
254: 
255: **Key Instruction.** Associates must always cross-reference the executed term sheet for the agreed-upon indemnification cap percentage. The term sheet is the governing benchmark for all commercial terms, and the indemnification cap is among the most carefully negotiated terms at the LOI stage. If the seller\'s draft SPA sets the general indemnification cap at a percentage different from what was agreed in the term sheet, this MUST be flagged immediately and corrected to match the term sheet. > \(f\) Changes affecting the industries in which the Company operates generally; and
